description: The image presents two side-by-side bar charts illustrating inter-annotator agreement, measured by Fleiss Kappa, compared to sample-level ambiguity standard deviation on the left and sample-level maximum ambiguity on the right. In the left chart, the horizontal axis contains the categories, labeled "Ambiguity Std," with categorical values ordered sequentially as 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, and 0.94. Its vertical value axis is labeled "Fleiss Kappa" and features a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to just above 0.8, with numeric tick marks spaced at intervals of 0.2. The left chart displays four bars rendered in varying shades of blue, each explicitly annotated with its exact numerical value directly above the bar. The tallest bar corresponds to the 0.0 category, shaded dark blue with an annotated value of 0.88; the bar for 0.47 is medium blue with a value of 0.46; the shortest bar represents the 0.82 category, colored light blue with a value of 0.03; and the bar for 0.94 is a slightly darker light blue with a value of 0.24. In the right chart, the horizontal axis contains the categories, labeled "Max Ambiguity," with numerical labels 1, 2, and 3 arranged in increasing order. The vertical axis mirrors the left chart, labeled "Fleiss Kappa" with a linear scale, a baseline of 0.0, and tick marks at 0.2 intervals. The right chart features three bars displaying a progressively descending height trend from left to right, shaded from dark to light blue. The tallest bar corresponds to category 1 with an annotated value of 0.89, the middle bar for category 2 has an annotated value of 0.46, and the shortest bar for category 3 has an annotated value of 0.23. Both charts visually emphasize the precise data points by utilizing bold text annotations for the exact values at the top of every bar.
